pharm: ATP-competitive inhibitor of all three AKT isoforms (AKT1/2/3); blocks PI3K/AKT signalling downstream of PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations
quick: 400 mg orally twice daily on days 1-4 of each week with fulvestrant
Can cause fetal harm; verify status; effective contraception during and after treatment per labeling
Do not breastfeed during treatment and after last dose per labeling
See full labeling; monitor renal function with diarrhoea/vomiting/dehydration risk
See full labeling; dose-reduce in moderate-severe impairment for hepatically cleared agents
No specific interaction; avoid excess with hepatotoxic or myelosuppressive therapy
CBC, LFTs, drug-specific toxicities, pregnancy status
summary: Capivasertib (Truqap) with fulvestrant is indicated for HR-positive HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alteration after endocrine-based therapy. Intermittent 4-days-on/3-days-off dosing manages hyperglycaemia and diarrhoea. Key toxicities are hyperglycaemia (including ketoacidosis risk in diabetics), diarrhoea, rash and embryo-fetal toxicity.
indications: HR-positive HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer with PIK3CA, AKT1 or PTEN alteration, in combination with fulvestrant, after progression on endocrine-based therapy

dosage.d: 400 mg twice daily on days 1-4 of each week of a 28-day cycle, with fulvestrant 500 mg IM days 1, 15, 29 then monthly
dosage.t: Take at the same times each dosing day, with or without food; swallow whole
dosage.n: 4-on/3-off schedule is integral - do not dose continuously

admin: Take exactly as prescribed; do not crush, split or chew unless labeling allows
Take at the same time(s) each day; if a dose is missed follow the missed-dose rule - do not double
Report interacting new medicines including antifungals, anti-TB drugs, antiepileptics and St John's wort (CYP3A4)
Store in the original container with desiccant where supplied; protect from moisture
moa: Capivasertib is an ATP-competitive inhibitor of all three AKT isoforms, blocking PI3K/AKT/mTOR signalling that drives growth in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered breast cancer. AKT also mediates insulin signalling, so hyperglycaemia is an on-target class effect.

relative: Diabetes mellitus or hyperglycaemia (monitor glucose closely; may need antihyperglycaemic therapy)
monitor: Fasting glucose/HbA1c before and during therapy

preg: No adequate human data. Based on mechanism, fetal harm is expected. Verify pregnancy status before starting; advise effective contraception during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose. Use in pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential fetal risk.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because of potential serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for the specified period after the last dose.
renal: Mild-moderate impairment: no routine change unless labeled; severe: limited data - monitor for exaggerated toxicity and dehydration-related AKI.
hepatic: Mild impairment: monitor; moderate-severe: dose-reduce or avoid per labeling (most agents hepatically cleared).

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (raise exposure - avoid or reduce to 320 mg BID per labeling)
moderate: Sensitive CYP3A4 substrates (capivasertib may alter exposure)
interactions.alcohol: Avoid excess alcohol with hepatotoxic therapy.
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference; monitor disease-specific markers.

serious: Hyperglycaemia including ketoacidosis risk in diabetics
emergency: Excessive thirst, frequent urination, fruity breath or confusion (possible severe hyperglycaemia) - seek emergency care
Severe diarrhoea with dizziness (dehydration) - seek urgent care

monitoring: Fasting glucose before starting and regularly; HbA1c in diabetics
counsel: Check blood sugar as instructed - this drug commonly raises glucose, especially if you have diabetes
Start anti-diarrhoea medicine at the first loose stool and call if it persists beyond a day
Report rash, mouth sores or vomiting that prevents eating/drinking
Take only on days 1-4 each week - mark a calendar; use contraception
pk: Target inhibition within hours-days; response assessed in weeks
Room temperature 20-25 C in original container; protect from moisture
pearls: Biomarker-selected: benefit confined to PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered tumours - test before starting
The 4-days-on/3-days-off rhythm is the tolerability strategy, not a missed-dose pattern
Hyperglycaemia is on-target (AKT mediates insulin signalling) - pre-empt in diabetics
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as remembered on the same day unless it is near the next dose; never double up. If a BID dose is missed by more than 4 hours, skip it; resume the 4-on/3-off rhythm.
overdose: No specific antidote. Withhold drug and give supportive care with monitoring of CBC, ECG, LFTs and agent-specific toxicities. Contact Poison Help (1-800-222-1222).
